In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the operating conditions of a pilot plant packed absorber and the mass transfer performance of three different packings.
the effects of three important operating parameters (liquid flow rate (L), flue gas flow rates (G) and regeneration temperature (T)) on CO 2 capture in an absorber packed with different packing.
the effects of three important operating parameters on CO 2 capture performance of the hybrid solvent MEA methanol.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hybrid solvent MEA-Methanol could be an effective solvent to absorb the CO 2 from the flue gas in a post-combustion capture process.
the hybrid solvent MEA-Methanol has a good CO 2 absorption performance and the Sulzer BX500 had the best mass-transfer performance.
the Sulzer BX500 was the optimal packing for CO 2 capture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Sulzer packing BX 500 is the best packing for CO2 absorption with hybrid solvent MEA-Methanol.

the optimal operating conditions for Sulzer BX500 were 40 L/h liquid flow rate, 5 m 2 /h flue gas flow and regeneration temperature 70 degC, for Mellapale Y 500 packing 500Y were 30 L/h liquid flow and 3 m 2 / h gas flow rate and for Pall rings 16x 16 were 30 L / h liquid flow rate and 3 m / h gas flow.
the orthogonal experiments are effective and feasible for the optimization of the operating parameters of the CO 2 absorption column packed with different packings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Sulzer BX500 has the best CO 2 absorption performance and the Mellapale Y-500 is better for the CO 2 absorption.
the CO2 absorption process with hybrid solvent of MEA-Methanol is more energy efficient than that of pure MEA solvent.
we have developed a new solvent system that can improve the CO 2 absorption rate and reduce the energy consumption.
